samples.sample_label: 0.04Nb steel aged at 723 K for 6 h

source.reason: The 0.04Nb steel strips were prepared by centrifugal casting under near-rapid solidification, which is the parent as-cast state of the 723 K/6 h aged sample.

processing_steps_notes.value: Ingot prepared by induction melting in a water-cooled copper crucible; re-melted and poured into a rotating copper mold at high speed to obtain steel strips of 60 × 70 × 2.5 mm under near-rapid solidification.

source.reason: Longer-period aging at 723 K (6 h) was conducted on the 0.04Nb steel; the aging setup (tubular vacuum furnace) is described in the Experimental section.

processing_steps_notes.value: Extended aging treatment at 723 K for 6 h conducted on both the 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels to investigate the effect of aging period on microstructure and mechanical properties.

source.reason: Microstructure of the 0.04Nb steel aged at 723 K for 6 h.

overall_structure.value: Two-phase microstructure consisting of austenite (γ) matrix with irregular δ-ferrite; intragranular nano-scale κ-carbides and submicron NbC particles are present. After aging at 723 K for 6 h, the primary phases remain ferrite and austenite with no observable new diffraction peak.

source.reason: XRD shows only ferrite and austenite after 723 K/6 h aging; SEM shows irregular ferrite in the austenite matrix and NbC particles; TEM shows intragranular κ-carbides.
XRD patterns show the primary phases remain ferrite and austenite with no new diffraction peak after 723 K aging.
Bulk microstructure of the 0.04Nb steel aged at 723 K for 6 h, from XRD, SEM and TEM characterization.
Ferrite content in the 0.04Nb steels aged at 723 K for 6 h is measured as 17.5 vol%.

morphology.value: irregular-shaped ferrite randomly dispersed in the austenite matrix; phase boundaries irregular with numerous irregular bulges

source.reason: SEM images show irregular-shaped ferrite in the austenite matrix, and with prolonged 723 K aging the ferrite/austenite phase boundaries become irregular with bulges.
κ-carbide precipitate data for the 0.04Nb steel aged at 723 K for 6 h from TEM characterization.

distribution.value: intragranular, dense and uniformly dispersed; volume fraction 18.7 vol%

source.reason: After aging at 723 K for 6 h, the κ-carbide volume fraction in the 0.04Nb steel increases to 18.7 vol% and the average size increases to 7 nm.
SAED insets in Figure 12 show the [100]γ // [100]κ orientation relationship for κ-carbides in the 0.04Nb steel aged at 723 K/6 h.
NbC particles are present in the 0.04Nb steel aged at 723 K; the particles are identified as NbC by TEM/EDS in the Nb-containing steels.

distribution.value: submicron white particles within the austenite matrix; size significantly increases with prolongation of aging period

source.reason: SEM images show submicron white NbC particles; compared to 0.02Nb steels, the NbC particle size in 0.04Nb steels significantly increases with longer aging.
Interface information for the 0.04Nb steel aged at 723 K for 6 h.
Phase boundaries between ferrite and austenite become irregular with numerous irregular bulges after prolonged 723 K aging.
SAED in Figure 12 shows the [100]γ // [100]κ orientation relationship, indicating a coherent κ-carbide/austenite interface in the 0.04Nb steel aged at 723 K/6 h.

phase_evolution.value: Prolonged 723 K aging promotes κ-carbide growth and coarsening; ferrite/austenite phase boundaries become irregular.

source.reason: Text states that prolonging aging treatment time promotes κ-carbide growth, and SEM shows irregular phase boundaries after prolonged aging.

interface_notes.value: No coarsened intergranular κ-carbides reported; only intragranular κ-carbides were characterized.

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the 0.04Nb steel strip (Table 1): Mn 12.82, Al 9.12, Cr 2.99, C 1.40, Nb 0.039, Fe Bal. (wt%).
For both the 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels, the aging treatment at 723 K for 6 h could result in good comprehensive mechanical properties.

Extended aging at 723 K does not markedly alter the yield strength of Nb-containing steels: κ-carbide precipitation strengthening intensifies while dislocation strengthening diminishes (grain boundary strengthening remains relatively unchanged).
Compared to 0.02Nb steels, the size of NbC particles in 0.04Nb steels significantly increases with the prolongation of aging period.
